text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu denied that Syria had called up its army reserves from Lebanon.
-Twelve hours of shelling into the Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridges.
-Israeli war planes broke the sound barrier in Naqoura as representatives of France, Israel, Lebanon, Syria and the United States met to discuss Lebanese and Israeli complaints.
-Foreign Minister Bouez: Netanyahu wants to blow up the peace process.
-Four pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army militiamen wounded inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
-National forces will meet today at the Riviera hotel to protest against the new law for audiovisual media. A number of stations are planning to defy the ban for one day.
-Acting Finance Minister Siniora: possible wage increases for public sector employees are not observed in the planned 1997 budget.
-Lebanese army commander General Lahoud inspected frontline units facing Israeli troops in south Lebanon and the Bekaa valley and ordered them to defend Lebanon by all possible means.
-Egypt's ambassador: Egypt is worried about the future of the peace process. Peace that is tailored to suit Israel is rejected.
